title: EST manifest (est.json), schema version 1
description: The manifest of an EST plugin bundle (EST specification §1), as Cyber's install reader (parseManifest) accepts it; a test proves the two agree. `est pack` fills module.sha256, module.bytes, ui.sha256 and assets from the files, so a plugin's source est.json may leave those out. Unknown keys are ignored. Lengths are in characters (the host counts UTF-16 code units: a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane counts twice there).

$schema.description: Where the schema is, for an editor (`./est-manifest-1.schema.json` in a folder `est new` made). `est pack` leaves it out of the bundle.

id.description: The plugin's id, a reverse-DNS name (`com.example.my-verb`), the same as its CLAP descriptor's. Never changed: projects name the plugin by it. (EST-M002)

name.description: The plugin's name as Cyber shows it. (EST-M004)

url.description: The plugin's web page, https only. (EST-M004)

license.description: An SPDX licence id or name (`MIT`). (EST-M004)

kind.description: An effect (audio in, audio out) or an instrument (notes in, audio out). (EST-M005)

features.description: CLAP feature names, the kind's first: `audio-effect` or `instrument`. (EST-M006)

est.description: The EST ABI edition: `1.0`, or (since Cyber 1.327) `1.1` for the fields EST 1.1 adds (a sidechain, up to 8 channels, `modulatable`, `ui.audio`, a preset's `image` and `author`). A newer edition is refused (EST-M019); a 1.1 field in a 1.0 manifest is refused (EST-M020).

path.description: The module's path in the bundle (`module.wasm`).

ui.description: A custom UI page, or null (or absent) for the generated UI. (EST-M009)

resizable.description: Read but unused in EST 1.0 (frame protocol 1 has no resize message): the host draws the frame at `size`, never scaled.

audio.description: EST 1.1 (frame protocol v3): the page may ask for an analysis of the plugin's output (`est.audio()`: magnitudes and RMS at most 30 times a second, never samples). (EST-M020)

assets.description: Every other file in the bundle, hashed. Written by `est pack`. (EST-M010)

sampleRates.description: Informational in EST 1.0: the host does not read it. The templates write "any": a plugin runs at the audio context's rate (44.1 or 48 kHz, whatever the device runs at) and must take whatever `activate` gives it.

audio.description: One main audio port each way at most; EST 1.1: an effect's inputs may add a sidechain after it. (EST-M011, EST-M021)

notes.description: Note ports: 0 or 1 each way; an instrument has a note input. (A value that is not an object is read as none.) (EST-M012)

limits.description: The most the plugin may use; the host holds it to them. (A value that is not an object is read as the defaults.) (EST-M013)

memoryPagesMax.description: 64 KiB pages; the module's declared maximum must be within it.

scale.description: How knobs, sliders and automation move over the parameter's range: "log" geometrically (a lane's midpoint is the geometric middle; the range the module reports must stay above 0, EST-C021). Since EST 1.286.

modulatable.description: EST 1.1: Cyber's clip envelopes may send this parameter `CLAP_EVENT_PARAM_MOD`; the DSP flags it `CLAP_PARAM_IS_MODULATABLE` (EST-C022). (EST-M020)

parameters.description: A mirror of the module's parameters: the same ids. (EST-M015)

stateVersion.description: The version of the state the plugin saves. (EST-M016)

presets.description: The bundle's preset index (`presets/index.json`), or null. (EST-M017)

compat.description: Informational in EST 1.0: Cyber's reader ignores it. The host versions the bundle is built for (the specification draft's plan: a bundle outside the range installs with a warning and runs).

host.description: A semver range of EST host versions; the templates write ">=1.0.0 <2".

from.description: The versions this entry applies to: comparators separated by spaces, all of which must hold (`>=1.0.0 <1.2.0`), a single version (that one only), or `*` (every version). Versions compare as semver (a pre-release before its release).

params.description: Old CLAP id (a decimal string) to new id (a renamed or split parameter: the value moves) or `null` (dropped on purpose). Every new id must be one `parameters` lists; an old id named by neither this map nor `parameters` is dropped with a note.

state.description: Whether the saved state (the CLAP state stream) crosses: `keep` (the plugin reads its earlier versions' state, CLAP's rule) or `drop` (the new version starts from its defaults on purpose, with the mapped values on top).

migrate.description: Since Cyber 1.337: what this version does with the settings a project saved with an earlier version. On Use installed version, Cyber applies the first entry whose `from` takes the version moved from and says what it kept, moved and dropped; without one, settings cross by id as before. A manifest with `migrate` lists its `parameters`. (EST-M022)
A manifest with `migrate` lists its parameters (EST-M022).

allOf.description: EST 1.1's fields only with `"abi": { "est": "1.1" }` (EST-M020); a second input is the sidechain (EST-M021).

path.description: A path in the bundle: `/`-separated segments of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, none `.` or `..`. (EST-B005)

channels.description: 1 or 2 in EST 1.0; up to 8 on a main port in EST 1.1 (an instrument's further pairs play on output strips; an effect's past two are summed into its stereo strip); a sidechain has 1 or 2.

role.description: EST 1.1: the first port is the main one; an effect's second input is the `"sidechain"`, fed from a track or a return. (EST-M021)
